_comment: Registry of setup levers, one entry per tunable: identity, value space, direction semantics, typical window, change effort, mechanism and recommendation target. value_source 'setup_sheet' means maps_to points into car.json; 'logged_data' means maps_to is null and the current value comes from a logged channel. Entries backed by a car_data.json table name it in 'notes'.

arb_fl.label: Front-Left ARB Position
arb_fl.mechanism: Sets the front axle's share of roll stiffness, hence its share of lateral load transfer and its grip relative to the rear.
arb_fl.notes: Stiffness from car_data.json arb.front: 6.3 N/mm (position 1) to 20.6 N/mm (position 7) at the drop link, ratio_to_wheel 1.07, monotonic, so 1 = softest. Whether stiffness scales linearly or squared with position is unknown (flagged convention_unresolved). Each corner is an independent target.

arb_fr.label: Front-Right ARB Position
arb_fr.mechanism: Sets the front axle's share of roll stiffness, hence its share of lateral load transfer and its grip relative to the rear.
arb_fr.notes: Stiffness from car_data.json arb.front; independent per-corner target.

arb_rl.label: Rear-Left ARB Position
arb_rl.mechanism: Sets the rear axle's share of roll stiffness, hence its share of lateral load transfer and its grip relative to the front.
arb_rl.notes: Stiffness from car_data.json arb.rear: 26.9 N/mm (position 1) to 80.1 N/mm (position 7) at the drop link, ratio_to_wheel 0.77, monotonic, so 1 = softest. Same convention_unresolved flag as the front.

arb_rr.label: Rear-Right ARB Position
arb_rr.mechanism: Sets the rear axle's share of roll stiffness, hence its share of lateral load transfer and its grip relative to the front.

springs_front.label: Front Springs
springs_front.mechanism: Sets axle ride stiffness independently of roll stiffness, and selects which damper window (car_data.json dampers.matrix_by_spring_pairing) applies.
springs_front.notes: Recommended damper windows depend on the installed spring pairing; see dampers.matrix_by_spring_pairing, cells keyed '{front}x{rear}'.

springs_rear.label: Rear Springs
springs_rear.mechanism: Sets axle ride stiffness independently of roll stiffness, and selects which damper window (car_data.json dampers.matrix_by_spring_pairing) applies.
springs_rear.notes: Conditions the damper matrix in the same way as springs_front.

damper_bump_ls_fl.label: FL Bump Low-Speed
damper_bump_ls_fl.adjustment_step_derived_from: Team practice: an exploratory change is 2 clicks (large enough to feel on track), a fine-tune change 1 click; the same for every damper adjuster.
damper_bump_ls_fl.change_effort_derived_from: Team setup-change overview: a damper change takes under 5 min in the pitlane without a setup patch, hence 'minutes'.
damper_bump_ls_fl.mechanism: Controls body motion into the damper (dive, roll rate at turn-in) - platform control.
damper_bump_ls_fl.notes: Click semantics from car_data.json dampers.dyno_metadata.front.click_semantics (the dyno chart's '0-0-0-0' and '18-18-18-18' reference curves). Team practice: axle-symmetric values, 1-2 click changes, bump and rebound moved independently.

damper_rebound_ls_fl.change_effort_derived_from: Team setup-change overview: a damper change takes under 5 min in the pitlane without a setup patch, hence 'minutes'.
damper_rebound_ls_fl.mechanism: Controls how fast the platform recovers after compression - controls floating.

ride_height_front.label: Front Ride Height
ride_height_front.adjustment_step_derived_from: One recommended ride-height step is 1 mm.
ride_height_front.mechanism: Sets front floor and splitter height above the ground (aero platform). FIA and aero conventions differ by a constant offset; aero wear means the measured value verifies the setting rather than being set independently.
ride_height_front.notes: Convention offsets in car_data.json ride_height_measuring_points (FIA/ADAC/Porsche laser, per corner X/Y/Z). Both readings move together, so neither is a free target.

ride_height_rear.label: Rear Ride Height
ride_height_rear.adjustment_step_derived_from: One recommended ride-height step is 1 mm.
ride_height_rear.mechanism: Sets rear floor and diffuser exit height, and with ride_height_front the rake; FIA and aero conventions differ by a constant offset.

diff_position.label: Differential Position
diff_position.mechanism: Sets clutch-pack preload, i.e. locking torque; more locking resists axle speed difference under power, trading exit rotation against traction.
diff_position.notes: Locking torque from car_data.json diff_locking_torque.positions (30-5 package: 1 -> 70 Nm to 5 -> 250 Nm, monotonic), so 1 = least. Torque per position drifts with wear. Per-corner engine braking weakens the diff in-corner and the engine-braking program is not in the data, which limits diff recommendations. Unit: the 5 sheet positions.

wing_position.label: Wing Position
wing_position.mechanism: Rear wing angle sets rear downforce: more angle gives more rear grip and stability at high speed, less top speed.
wing_position.notes: Legal positions from car_data.json wing_position_table, 'GT3 R 2026' column: only 7.3/8.3/9.3 deg (P8/P9/P10).

toe_front.label: Front Toe
toe_front.mechanism: Front toe-out sharpens initial turn-in at the cost of straight-line stability and tyre wear.
toe_front.notes: No car_data table backs this lever; value space and direction are team knowledge.

toe_rear.label: Rear Toe
toe_rear.mechanism: Rear toe-in adds straight-line and exit stability at the cost of some rear tyre wear.
toe_rear.notes: Team knowledge only, no car_data table (as toe_front).

camber_fl.label: FL Camber
camber_fl.adjustment_step_derived_from: Team practice: a camber change is two 0.1 deg clicks (0.2 deg).
camber_fl.mechanism: Sets static camber, chosen from tyre usage and temperature distribution across the contact patch.
camber_fl.notes: Base -3.5 deg front. Team knowledge only, no car_data table. One click = 0.1 deg, a typical change two clicks. A tyre-surface and wear-pattern check precedes any change; a single-corner change is sometimes preferred over the symmetric pair. Takes 20-30 min (half_hour).

camber_fr.notes: Base -3.5 deg front. Team knowledge only, no car_data table. One click = 0.1 deg, a typical change two clicks. A tyre-surface and wear-pattern check precedes any change; a single-corner change is sometimes preferred over the symmetric pair. Takes 20-30 min (half_hour).

tc_lat.label: Traction Control - Lateral

value_space.feasible_derived_from: The manufacturer TC table is monotonic only from 2 to 11 (0 and 1 are not on the same scale), so a decrease from 2 is at the limit.

direction_semantics.1: driver modulation, minimal TC support (wording near-identical to 0; the scale is not cleanly monotonic between 0/1 and 2 -- see notes)
direction_semantics.increasing_2_to_11: LESS permitted car rotation under lateral load on power = MORE TC intervention/support

tc_lat.mechanism: Sets how much rotation TC permits while power is applied in the cornering phase; a higher position permits less rotation (more intervention).
tc_lat.notes: Driver-adjustable from the steering wheel; the current value is logged, not on the setup sheet, and stays not assessable because the LAT/LON mapping of ecu_B_tc_act is undocumented. Direction from car_data.json tc (current LAT/LON system): from 2 ('even more rotation') to 11 ('lots of TC support') monotonically less rotation, the opposite of a naive 'higher = more rotation' reading. Position 1 reads almost like 0 and is flagged, not smoothed.

tc_lon.label: Traction Control - Longitudinal

value_space.feasible_derived_from: The manufacturer TC table is monotonic only from 2 to 11 (0 and 1 are not on the same scale), so a decrease from 2 is at the limit.

direction_semantics.0: driver modulation, little TC support -- NOTE: per project docs, TC LON at 0 does NOT disable TC (only TC LAT=0 does); wording matches position 1
direction_semantics.increasing_2_to_11: LESS permitted wheel spin under longitudinal load = MORE TC intervention/support

tc_lon.mechanism: Sets how much wheel spin TC permits in high-torque phases (1st/2nd gear power-down on exit); a higher position permits less spin, which helps manage rear-tyre degradation.
tc_lon.notes: Driver-adjustable from the steering wheel; current value not assessable (see tc_lat). Direction from car_data.json tc: monotonically less wheel spin from 2 to 11, 5 = baseline. TC LON = 0 does not switch TC off; only TC LAT has an off state.

abs_position.label: ABS Position

direction_semantics.type: categorical, NOT a single monotonic soft/hard axis
direction_semantics.1_to_8: dry maps -- 1-4 grouped 'High' overall grip level (1=baseline dry-high, 2/4=more stable FA/RA variants, 3=printed 'BL Medium grip map' despite its own row being categorised 'High' -- verified as printed, not a transcription error), 5-8 grouped 'Medium' overall grip level (5=baseline medium, 6=more stable, 7-8=add lateral support)
direction_semantics.9_to_11: wet maps ascending severity -- 9=baseline good-wet-grip, 10=rain tyres/heavy wet (limited deceleration), 11=monsoon emergency (highly limited deceleration)

abs_position.mechanism: Selects the ABS intervention map; in practice a sweet-spot search within the dry or wet bracket, not a linear soft-to-hard sweep.
abs_position.notes: Driver-adjustable from the steering wheel; the current value comes from the logged channel log_abs_pos, which agrees with log_rt_abs_pos and stw_rt04_abs (the ECU-side abs_switch_pos does not; see channels.json). Installed map set V2, table in car_data.json abs. Categorical: jumping between grip-level brackets is not a tuning move; within a bracket a +1/+2 step nudges toward the front- or rear-axle-stable variant.

brake_bias.label: Brake Bias

value_space.note: Direction convention (forward vs rear) and the channel itself are not identified, so not set here.

brake_bias.mechanism: Driver-only in-corner adjustment, braking-phase target. Its current value cannot be evaluated until the bias channel is identified.
brake_bias.notes: Recommendation target behind the lockup chain (Segers C5-1/2). The value is logged, not on the setup sheet; with no identified channel, direction_semantics stays null and typical_window not assessable.

splitter_offset.label: Splitter Offset

direction_semantics.hard_limit: the NEGATIVE extreme (more front downforce) is bounded by front-splitter/track contact, track-dependent -- HARD edge. The positive extreme is a range limit only, no physical contact -- SOFT edge. Author-elicited 2026-09-22 (Phase C), resolving Phase A's own unresolved placeholder ('sign convention unresolved, not invented, flagged for elicitation') -- see thesis_notes.md for the full provenance record.

splitter_offset.mechanism: Front aero balance trim for high-speed balance; paired with wing_position (same aero axis) and ride_height_front (shared ground clearance).
splitter_offset.notes: A change takes about 2 min roughly or 20 min precisely (minutes). The offset-to-effect relation is not digitised. Negative = more front downforce, positive = less; negative approaches a hard edge (splitter/track contact), positive only a range limit. Simplification: setup_state._window_edge_check treats both value_space ends as hard.
